title: Neil Marine strengthens boat building capacity with new Dikovita yard | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 00:09
-     - 0

Neil Marine Group has expanded its boatbuilding operations with a new Rs. 50 million-plus manufacturing facility at Dikovita, Wattala, as the company seeks to increase production, create jobs and strengthen Sri Lanka’s position in the international boatbuilding market.

The new yard, approved by the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka, has been established on previously abandoned land belonging to the Ceylon Fishery Harbours Corporation.

The project represents a  public-private partnership aimed at putting underutilised state assets to productive use while expanding private-sector manufacturing capacity.

The company described the facility as a new chapter in its manufacturing journey, with its broader ambition captured in the message: “Built in Sri Lanka. Exported to the world.”

The facility was recently opened with religious observances led by the Maha Sangha under the patronage of the Incumbent of Ratmalana Mallikaramaya, Ven. Pandita Ranasgalle Gnanaweera Thero.

The occasion also paid tribute to the late Neil Fernando, founder of Neil Marine Group, whose vision helped build the company into a recognised name in Sri Lanka’s boatbuilding industry over more than five decades.

The Dikovita yard is expected to provide additional production capacity for Neil Marine and support the company’s plans to expand its presence in export markets. The company said the investment would contribute to higher export earnings and generate new employment opportunities.

Operations at the facility are headed by Officer-in-Charge Ajith Susantha and his team, under the leadership of Group Chairman Kumari Fernando, Group President Manel Fernando and CEO Shan Perera.

Deputy Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources Minister Rathna Gamage, Industries’ Ministry Boatbuilding Sector Chairman Indra Kaushal Rajapaksha, representatives of the Export Development Board and other Government and industry officials attended the opening.

The investment comes as Sri Lanka seeks to develop higher-value manufacturing industries capable of generating foreign exchange and employment, while reducing dependence on traditional export sectors.

For Neil Marine, the new facility is also intended to reinforce the company’s role in an industry with potential for greater export diversification. The company plans to use the Dikovita site as a production base for boats serving both domestic and overseas markets.

title: Sri Lanka Expo 2027 promotional event in Melbourne highlights investment and trade opportunities | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 00:07
-     - 0

The Consulate General of Sri Lanka in Melbourne organised a “Sri Lanka Expo 2027” promotional event on 14 August at the Consulate, bringing together Australian and Sri Lankan business stakeholders to explore trade, investment and business opportunities in Sri Lanka.

The event was attended by Export Development Board Chairman Mangala Wijesinghe and Board of Investment of Sri Lanka Director General Dr. Sulakshana Jayawardena.

The program provided Victoria-based business leaders and importers with first-hand information on investment opportunities, export potential and incentives available to international investors in Sri Lanka.

Victoria-based companies interested in participating in Sri Lanka Expo 2027 attended the program, representing sectors including food and beverage, logistics, financial services, tourism and wellness. Victoria-based importers of leading Sri Lankan food and beverage brands also participated, providing an opportunity to discuss challenges affecting bilateral trade between Sri Lanka and Australia.

Addressing the participants, Consul General, Pradeepa Saram highlighted Sri Lanka Expo 2027, to be held at the Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall (BMICH), Colombo, from 14–17 January 2027, as one of the country’s largest international business events and invited Australian and Sri Lankan business entities to use the Expo as a platform to establish new partnerships and explore business opportunities in Sri Lanka.

EDB Chairman Wijesinghe made a detailed presentation on EXPO-2027, outlining opportunities for international buyers, exporters and investors to connect with Sri Lankan companies and develop commercial partnerships. He also highlighted the advantages arising from Sri Lanka’s existing Free Trade Agreements and preferential trade arrangements with India, Pakistan, Singapore and Thailand, and explained how Australian investors could leverage Sri Lanka’s trade relationships and strategic location to access regional markets.

BOI Director General Dr. Jayawardena briefed participants on investment opportunities in Sri Lanka, particularly in the industry, energy and mineral sectors, and explained the investor-friendly packages, incentives and other benefits available to foreign investors seeking to establish or expand operations in Sri Lanka. He further highlighted the new digital investment platform launched by the BOI to facilitate and attract foreign investment.

The discussion also focused on practical challenges faced by Victoria-based importers of Sri Lankan products, particularly lengthy procedures for obtaining Plant Quarantine and phytosanitary certification.

In response, EDB Chairman Wijesinghe assured participants that a meeting would be convened with the relevant agencies to identify solutions and streamline the process.

The promotional event underscored the Consulate General’s continued efforts to strengthen Sri Lanka–Australia trade and investment relations and expand business-to-business engagement.

title: Chathuranga visits Custom Denning facilities in Sydney | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 00:04
-     - 1

Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe, conducted an official visit to Custom Denning’s electric bus manufacturing facility in St Marys, Sydney, on 17 August 2026.

The visit aimed to observe advanced zero-emission transit technology and explore potential avenues for industrial collaboration, technology transfer, and advanced manufacturing.

The Deputy Minister was accompanied by Deputy High Commissioner of Sri Lanka, Wishwanath Aponsu. The delegation was received by  Custom Denning Managing Director Scott Dunn, Chief Operating Officer, Daniel Bale, and Financial Controller, Niro Bandara.

The engagement followed preliminary discussions facilitated by the Sri Lanka High Commission in Canberra during the official visit of Foreign Affairs Minister Vijith Herath, in June.

The visit underscores the growing diplomatic and trade interest between Sri Lanka and Australia.

title: Abans joins Dialog Pay merchant ecosystem | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 00:00
-     - 1

From left: Dialog Axiata Group Chief Operating Officer Lim Li San, Dialog Finance Business Officer Sachini De Silva, Abans Senior Brand Manager Samith Fernando, and Head of Finance Nandun Wickramasighe

Dialog Axiata PLC has announced its partnership with Abans, enabling customers to make secure LankaQR payments using Dialog Pay across all Abans showrooms island-wide. The partnership extends digital payment convenience to one of Sri Lanka’s leading retail brands, with a network of over 400 outlets, while rewarding customers with complimentary Dialog data on eligible LankaQR transactions.

Customers can now use Dialog Pay to purchase a wide range of products, including consumer electronics, home appliances, mobile devices, IT products, furniture, kitchen appliances and other lifestyle solutions available at Abans showrooms nationwide. The partnership provides customers with a secure and convenient way to pay while enjoying greater flexibility when shopping for everyday essentials and high-value purchases alike.

Abans Head of Finance Nandun Wickramasighe said, ”At Abans, we are committed to continuously enhancing the shopping experience by offering our customers greater convenience, choice and flexibility. Our partnership with Dialog Pay introduces another trusted digital payment option across our retail network, making it easier for customers to shop the products they need. By bringing together two trusted brands, we are helping accelerate the adoption of digital payments while supporting Sri Lanka’s transition towards a more digitally enabled economy.”

Dialog Pay, available through the Dialog Pay App and the MyDialog App, brings together connectivity, digital payments and financial services within a single ecosystem, supporting Dialog’s vision of making digital payments simpler, more accessible and more rewarding for every Sri Lankan. Customers can conveniently activate Dialog Pay using their eZ Cash account or by linking their preferred bank account, enabling them to make secure LankaQR payments, transfer funds, access their digital wallet, open savings accounts and fixed deposits, and apply for loans powered by Dialog Finance. Accepted across more than 100,000 retail outlets nationwide, Dialog Pay rewards eligible QR payments with complimentary Dialog data, encouraging greater everyday adoption while supporting Sri Lanka’s continued transition towards a more digitally connected and cash-light economy.
